facts: Training/inference decoder receives an image-derived observable_sheet_half_extent from alpha bounding boxes rather than exact camera.json half_extent.
An audited master witness has exact camera half_extent 0.54 in V0 and V2.
For that witness V2 alpha support span is 948/1024, giving observable half_extent 0.5400843882, approximately matching 0.54.
camera_scale_input.limitation: Known camera scale should not be re-derived from style pixels. V2 should feed exact camera authority directly and treat this as an explicit apparatus change.

facts: S1 membership must remain interpreted exactly as run; later clean-character findings cannot retroactively reinterpret S1.
The parallel Geppetto/Arachne corpus audit has demonstrated that structural eligibility does not guarantee a semantically clean single-character render.
Automatic clean-C0 audit is still being completed and will receive blind/random visual sanity checks.
corpus_substrate.next_experiment_rule: The first decoder-only causal comparison must keep S1 membership fixed. Clean-C0 is a separate H0 intervention, not combined with the decoder intervention.

facts: Dense evaluation queries every authoritative visible raster row.
Predicted P is reconstructed with exact camera.json forward/right/up and exact half_extent.
DTB-ND1 robust local-plane route and frozen Geppetto/Arachne proxies are used.
FIT eligibility is 27/32 families =54 style cells with pass minimum 52; TRAIN eligibility is 28/32=56 style cells with pass minimum 54.
Ineligible families are neither PASS nor FAIL; hard route failures among eligible cells are forbidden.
Scalar depth diagnostics do not substitute for direct consumer replay.
Loss is FP32 mean SmoothL1 with beta=0.01 over selected visible loci.
At |e|<beta, gradient magnitude is |e|/beta; e=0.002 therefore gives 0.2 and e=0.0002 gives 0.02.
For |e|>=0.01 the SmoothL1 gradient magnitude saturates at 1.
AdamW uses betas=(0.9,0.95), weight_decay=0; LR 3e-4 steps 1-2048, fresh AdamW moments and LR 3e-5 from 2049-32768.
AMP FP16 shared stack, FP32 targets/loss, GradScaler; four 4-cell microbatches accumulate one 16-cell logical update.
Resume saves/restores model, optimizer, scaler and Python/NumPy/Torch CPU/CUDA RNG state.
limitations: Mean pointwise loss is not aligned to the frozen consumer's tail/derivative sensitivity.
Global deterministic algorithms are deliberately not forced because CUDA grid_sample backward may be nondeterministic.
S and B are single executions; tiny count differences such as TRAIN 17->18 must not be interpreted as a reliable ranking without repeatability calibration.

facts: DINO source revision is sealed to 7764ea0f912e53c92e82eb78a2a1631e92725fc8 and official weight hashes are runtime checked.
Input is RGBA 1024 contract but DINO preprocess uses RGB only, bicubic+antialias resize to 518, ImageNet normalization.
Only last-layer x_norm_patchtokens are cached, shape 37x37 x native_dim, FP32 lossless; Q_d zero-pad to 1536 then per-token FP32 L2.
Cache files are hash checked and lossless roundtrip checked.
No multi-layer or multiscale DINO access exists.
limitations: 37x37 token grid corresponds to about 27.7 native pixels per token axis after 1024->518->patch14; subpatch detail must come through the native path.
Last-layer-only access can hide useful earlier-layer local detail; this is an interface hypothesis, not a proven cause.

facts: Exactly 4096 raster rows per view are selected deterministically.
When visible rows >=4096, sampling is uniform without replacement; when <4096, deterministic coverage-repeat is used.
Every view receives exactly 4096 loss slots, so view weighting is equal rather than proportional to visible area.
No augmentation, hard mining, silhouette/edge/thin/grazing stratification or mechanics-derived weighting is used.
limitations: Empirical sampling coverage by silhouette distance, thin structure and grazing geometry was not measured before S1.
Uniform visible-row sampling can underrepresent mechanically sensitive low-area structures.

facts: Local DINO field remains 37x37; it is incorrect to claim all DINO information is reduced to 16x16.
Cross-view context is pooled 37->16, fused across view-row sequences, then bilinearly upsampled 16->37.
Every rung enters the same trainable 1536->256 stem.
Total trainable parameters are 5,046,739.
Native encoder has 29,640 parameters (0.587% of total) and sees only 25 RGBA samples per query at center plus radii 1,4,16.
Final depth decoder has 133,643 parameters (2.648% of total) and predicts each query pointwise after bilinear feature sampling.
shared_learner_access.interpretation: This architecture can impose a common high-resolution accessibility ceiling and therefore confound a backbone-scale ladder. It is a plausible mechanism, not yet a causal proof.

forbidden_claims: The shared decoder/access path has already been causally proven to be the dominant failure source.
Loss is proven secondary to decoder.
permitted_claims: S1 S->B flatness is conditional on SharedLearnerV1 and its frozen training/evaluation apparatus.
SharedLearnerV1 contains material high-resolution access limitations that justify stopping the capacity ladder and testing the apparatus first.
The evaluator route itself passed the code-level authority audit.
required_before_next_training: Version and freeze a high-resolution spatial decoder/native-access V2 while keeping current loss fixed for the first causal test.
Use exact camera.json half_extent instead of alpha-derived scale proxy.
Preregister DINO ON/native ON, DINO OFF/native ON and DINO ON/native OFF as separately trained/evaluated conditions.
Add a repeatability calibration or deterministic substitute sufficient to bound run-to-run noise before interpreting small deltas.
Do not change beta or add tail loss in the decoder-only experiment.
After decoder causality: beta-only ablation, then tail/CVaR-only ablation with beta fixed.
Do not reopen S/B/L/g until a single rung shows adequate accessibility through the revised apparatus.
scope: S1 frozen representation/cache, sampling/supervision, shared learner/access, loss/optimizer/runtime, evaluator, camera-scale input, corpus substrate
